topics.title: Recognising Coins and Notes
topics.concept:
What is Money?

Money is what we use to buy things we need or want. In India, money comes in the form of coins and notes (paper money).

Indian Coins:

CoinColourShapeWho is on it?
₹1SilverRoundNew Rupee symbol
₹2SilverRoundNew Rupee symbol
₹5Silver/GoldRound with edgesNew Rupee symbol
₹10Silver/GoldRoundNew Rupee symbol
₹20Silver12-sidedNew Rupee symbol

Indian Notes (Paper Money):

NoteColourPicture on it
₹10Orange-brownSun Temple, Konark
₹20GreenEllora Caves
₹50CyanHampi with Chariot
₹100LavenderRani Ki Vav
₹200YellowSanchi Stupa
₹500Stone greyRed Fort
₹2000MagentaMangalyaan

Important Points:

  • The symbol for Indian Rupee is ₹
  • Coins are made of metal; notes are made of paper (special paper)
  • Each coin and note has a different value

examples.solution:
• ₹5 coin is silver/gold in colour
  • It is medium-sized

-

Answer: The ₹5 coin **Example 2:** What colour is the ₹50 note? *Solution:* - ₹50 note is cyan (blue-green) in colour - It has a picture of Hampi with a chariot - **Answer:** Cyan **Example 3:** Name two coins that are silver in colour. *Solution:* - ₹1 coin is silver - ₹2 coin is also silver - **Answer:** ₹1 and ₹2 coins

topics.title: Counting Money and Simple Buying
topics.concept:
How to Count Money:

Add the values of all coins and notes together to find the total amount.

Counting Coins:

  • ₹1 + ₹1 = ₹2
  • ₹2 + ₹2 = ₹4
  • ₹5 + ₹5 = ₹10
  • ₹10 + ₹10 = ₹20

Counting Notes:

  • ₹10 + ₹10 = ₹20
  • ₹20 + ₹20 = ₹40
  • ₹50 + ₹50 = ₹100
  • ₹100 + ₹100 = ₹200

Adding Different Coins and Notes:

  • ₹5 coin + ₹2 coin = ₹7
  • ₹10 note + ₹5 coin = ₹15
  • ₹20 note + ₹10 note + ₹5 coin = ₹35

Simple Buying (Paying and Change):

  • When you buy something, you give money to the shopkeeper
  • If you give more than the price, you get change back
  • Change = Money given − Price of item

Example: A toy costs ₹15. You give ₹20. Change = ₹20 − ₹15 = ₹5.

examples.problem: Count the money: ₹10 note + ₹5 coin + ₹2 coin = ?
examples.solution:
• Add step by step: ₹10 + ₹5 = ₹15
  • ₹15 + ₹2 = ₹17

-

Answer: ₹17 **Example 2:** A chocolate costs ₹25. You give a ₹50 note. How much change do you get? *Solution:* - Change = Money given − Price - ₹50 − ₹25 = ₹25 - **Answer:** ₹25 change **Example 3:** Sam has a ₹20 note and two ₹5 coins. How much money does he have in total? *Solution:* - Two ₹5 coins = ₹5 + ₹5 = ₹10 - Total = ₹20 + ₹10 = ₹30 - **Answer:** ₹30

recap: Count money by adding values of coins and notes
Price = cost of the item you want to buy
Change = money given − price (if you give more)
Always check if you have enough money before buying
Practice adding small amounts to become faster

topics.title: Real-Life Money Activities and Currency Awareness
topics.concept:
Real-Life Money Activities:

ActivityWhat You DoMath Skill
**Buying a snack**Give money, get changeSubtraction
**Saving in a piggy bank**Collect coins, count totalAddition
**Comparing prices**See which item costs lessComparing numbers
**Grocery shopping**Add prices of multiple itemsAddition
**Checking if you have enough**Compare money with priceComparing

Steps for Buying Something:

1. Look at the price of the item

2. Count the money you have

3. If money ≥ price, you can buy it

4. Give money to the shopkeeper

5. If money > price, you get change

Currency Awareness:

  • Different countries use different money
  • India uses the Indian Rupee (₹)
  • USA uses the US Dollar ($)
  • UK uses the British Pound (£)
  • Europe uses the Euro (€)

Saving Money Tips for Kids:

  • Save coins in a piggy bank
  • Keep track of how much you save
  • Set a goal (e.g., save ₹100 for a toy)
  • Spend wisely - not all at once!

examples.problem: Riya has ₹35. She wants to buy a pen for ₹20 and a notebook for ₹15. Does she have enough money?
examples.solution:
• Total cost = ₹20 + ₹15 = ₹35
  • Riya has ₹35
  • ₹35 = ₹35, so she has exactly enough

-

Answer: Yes, she has enough money **Example 2:** A toy costs ₹60. Rohan has a ₹50 note and a ₹20 note. How much money does he have? Can he buy the toy? *Solution:* - Total money = ₹50 + ₹20 = ₹70 - Toy costs ₹60 - ₹70 > ₹60, so he can buy it - Change = ₹70 − ₹60 = ₹10 - **Answer:** Yes, he can buy it and will get ₹10 change **Example 3:** Name the currency used in (a) India (b) USA *Solution:* - India uses the Indian Rupee (₹) - USA uses the US Dollar ($) - **Answer:** (a) Rupee (b) Dollar

recap: Buying requires giving money and possibly getting change
Always check if you have enough money before buying
Saving money in a piggy bank helps reach goals
Practice real-life shopping scenarios to learn money skills
